item.title: Easy Kale Salad
item.dc:creator: Beth Moncel
item.description:
This easy Kale Salad is tangy, sweet, and crunchy with Granny Smith apples, walnuts, raisins, and a homemade Dijon vinaigrette.

The post Easy Kale Salad appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
I’m in love. The dressing alone on this easy Kale Salad is enough to make me swoon. It’s just a very simple Dijon vinaigrette, but it tastes so good with the earthy kale, crunchy walnuts, crisp apple, and juicy raisins. This salad is fresh, tangy, sweet, genuinely EASY, and makes some very budget-friendly ingredients taste just downright delicious. And because kale is so sturdy, it stands up well to being pre-dressed with the vinaigrette, making this salad great for weekly meal prep!

“This is so good! I’m not usually a big fan of raw kale, but the dressing made it one of the best salads I’ve had, kale or not. And thanks for the tip on cutting up kale; I’m not very experienced with food prep, and those kinds of details have made the recipes on your site so much easier for me!”

Elise

Fresh, Crunchy, and Perfect for Meal Prep

For the longest time, kale and I had a slightly complicated relationship. Not because I didn’t like it, because I do! But I mostly saved it for cooked dishes, and I never seemed to finish the whole bunch before it started looking a little worse for wear in the back of my fridge. Whenever I ate it raw, the leaves felt a little too firm and bitter unless I let it sit with the dressing on for a bit. But sometimes I wanted to dig into my kale salad right away!

The problem wasn’t the kale. I had been skipping the step that makes raw kale so much more enjoyable. I used to think massaging kale was an unnecessary extra step, but then I tried it, and now I understand why people do it. It only takes a few minutes, but it really does help soften the sturdy leaves and mellow their bitter edge. It also makes it easier for them to soak up that delicious Dijon dressing. Add in a tart but juicy Granny Smith apple, some crunchy walnuts, and a handful of sweet raisins, and this easy kale salad completely changed the way I felt about eating kale raw. Trust me on this one.

Recipe Success Tips

  1. Remove the thick stems and chop the kale into small pieces. The thick, woody stems stay tough even after the kale is massaged and dressed. I like to strip those away before chopping the leaves into small bite-sized pieces. However, don’t throw the stems away! They’re delicious added to a veggie stir fry later.
  2. Use pre-chopped kale to save time. Pre-chopped bagged kale is pretty easy to find these days and fairly inexpensive (since it doesn’t wilt quickly), so I‘m quite happy to pay for this convenience when the price is right!
  3. Dry the kale well! After washing the kale, I always make sure it’s as dry as possible before adding the dressing. Extra water can dilute the vinaigrette and keep it from clinging to the leaves. I usually run my kale through a salad spinner. If you don’t have a salad spinner, spread the kale out on a clean kitchen towel or some paper towels and pat it dry.
  4. Add the dressing a little at a time. I start by tossing the kale with about half of the Dijon vinaigrette, then add more until it’s dressed the way I like it (I usually end up adding it all). Since the dressing is fairly apple cider vinegar-forward, some readers prefer a lighter coating. You can stir in 1 teaspoon of honey into the dressing for a little less tang, if you like!

Massage Your Kale!

Yep, massage those greens and taste the difference! Kale leaves are naturally sturdy and fibrous, so giving them a quick massage helps soften their texture before you eat them raw. You’ll be able to SEE and feel the kale change right in the bowl.

So why should you massage kale, anyway?

  • It softens the leaves. Gently squeezing and rubbing the kale helps break down some of its tough and fibrous structure. This makes it feel tender instead of chewy in your mouth.
  • It mellows the flavor. I’m sure we can all agree that kale can taste pretty bitter. Massaging the leaves helps break down the compounds that give it those qualities. If you massage it with an acid (like apple cider vinegar, which I use in this recipe) and/or salt, it actually chemically alters the greens and mellows out the flavor!
  • It works in the dressing. Because you’re working the oil, vinegar, and seasonings into the kale, it coats the leaves more evenly instead of sliding off and collecting at the bottom of the bowl.

How to massage kale:

  1. Remove the stems: Strip away the thick, woody stems (some thinner stems are ok), then chop or tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces.
  2. Add some of the dressing: Drizzle the kale with half the Dijon vinaigrette.
  3. Get your hands in there: Using clean hands, grab and gently squeeze handfuls of kale, working your way around the bowl so all the leaves get some attention. I like to rub a few of the firmer pieces lightly between my fingers, too. There will be a noticeable difference from when you start to when you’re done!
  4. Watch for the change: After 1-3 minutes, the kale should look darker and glossier, shrink to about half its original size, and feel noticeably softer.

Easy Kale Salad

This easy Kale Salad is tangy, sweet, and crunchy with Granny Smith apples, walnuts, raisins, and a homemade Dijon vinaigrette.
Course Salad
Cuisine American
Total Cost $5.90 recipe / $1.48 serving
Prep Time 20 minutes minutes
Total Time 20 minutes minutes
Servings 4 servings
Calories 335kcal
Author Beth Moncel

Equipment

  • Mixing Bowls

Ingredients

For the Kale Salad

  • ½ lb. chopped kale about one bunch, $1.24*
  • 1 medium granny smith apple $0.90
  • 1 lemon optional, $0.68**
  • ½ cup walnut halves 50g, $1.25
  • ¼ cup raisins 35g, $0.47

For the Dijon Vinaigrette

  • ¼ cup apple cider vinegar 60ml, $0.15
  • 1 clove garlic minced, (½ tsp) $0.07
  • 1½ Tbsp Dijon mustard $0.09
  • ¼ tsp salt $0.01
  • ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked, $0.04
  • ⅓ cup olive oil 79ml, $1.00

Instructions

  • Gather your ingredients.
  • Remove and discard the thick stems from the kale. Chop or tear the leaves into smaller pieces. Rinse the kale well under cool running water, then dry it thoroughly in a salad spinner or with a clean kitchen towel.
  • Chop the Granny Smith apple into bite-sized pieces. For extra protection against browning, place the apple in a small bowl, squeeze the lemon juice over it, and toss to coat. This step is optional, but recommended for meal prepping.
  • Add the apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and freshly cracked pepper to a bowl. Whisk until combined. Slowly stream in the olive oil, whisking constantly, until the vinaigrette is smooth and emulsified. Alternatively, blend all the dressing ingredients together until smooth. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper as needed.
  • Add the kale to a large bowl and pour half of the Dijon vinaigrette over top. Using clean hands, gently massage the dressing into the kale for 1-3 minutes, or until the leaves look darker and glossier and feel noticeably softer.
  • Add the walnuts, prepared apple, and raisins to the kale, then toss until evenly combined.
  • Taste the salad and add more vinaigrette as desired (I used the whole batch). Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to eat.

See how we calculate recipe costs here.

Notes

*I used curly kale in this recipe as it’s affordable and easy to find, but dinosaur (lacinato) kale works just as well. You can also use pre-chopped bagged kale to save a little prep time (use ½ lb.)
**The lemon juice is optional, but it keeps the apples bright and prevents them from browning. It also helps keep the kale bright green and assists with the overall fresh flavor of the dressing. You can discard the leftover lemon juice after you’ve tossed the diced apples, or just add it to the bowl if you like a little more tang in your salad dressing! (I do.)
Storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. I don’t recommend freezing this salad because the apples lose their texture after thawing, and the dressing and kale become watery and limp.

Nutrition

Serving: 1serving | Calories: 335kcal | Carbohydrates: 19g | Protein: 5g | Fat: 29g | Sodium: 242mg | Fiber: 5g

How to Make Kale Salad Step-by-Step Photos

Gather all of your ingredients.

Prep and wash the kale: Remove and discard the thick, woody stems from ½ lb. kale. A few of the thinner stems are fine to leave behind. I just run my hands down the stem and pull the leaves as I go, as shown here.

Now tear the kale into smaller pieces. I like using smaller pieces of kale in fresh salads because it makes the kale easier to chew and eat. If I’m cooking kale, I generally leave it in larger pieces. Place the chopped kale in a colander and rinse well under cool running water.

Dry the kale: Before you build the salad, make sure the kale is as dry as possible. Give it a spin in a salad spinner until there’s very little water collecting in the bottom. No salad spinner? Shake off as much water as you can, spread the kale over a clean kitchen towel or paper towels, and gently pat it dry. The drier the leaves are, the better that AH-MAZING dressing will cling!

Prep the apple: Core and chop 1 medium Granny Smith apple into small, bite-sized pieces and halve the lemon (if using).

For extra insurance against browning, place the apple in a small bowl and squeeze the juice from 1 lemon over top. Toss until all the pieces are lightly coated. This step is optional, but it’s especially handy if you’re meal prepping the salad.

Make the dressing: Now it’s time to make the dressing. Add ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, 1 finely minced garlic clove, 1½ Tbsp Dijon mustard, ¼ tsp salt, and ¼ tsp freshly cracked pepper to a small bowl. Whisk until the mustard is fully mixed in and no streaks remain.

Slowly stream ⅓ cup olive oil into the vinegar mixture, whisking constantly. The vinaigrette should become slightly thicker and look smooth rather than separated. You can also add all the dressing ingredients to a blender and blend until the garlic is minced and the dressing is smooth.

Taste the dressing and adjust the salt or pepper if you’d like. If you find the dressing too tangy, whisk in about 1 tsp honey or some sugar to tone it down. But I suggest keeping it pretty tangy because that bright flavor works so well with the sweet raisins and apple.

Massage the kale: Place the dry kale in a large bowl and pour about half of the Dijon vinaigrette over top.

Get your hands in there and gently grab, squeeze, and rub handfuls of kale, moving around the bowl so every leaf gets some attention. Continue massaging for 1-3 minutes. You’ll know it’s ready when the leaves look darker and glossier, have reduced slightly in volume, and feel noticeably softer between your fingers. Stop once the kale is tender but still has some texture. You don’t want to massage it into mush!

Assemble the salad: Now add ½ cup walnuts, the prepared apple, and ¼ cup raisins to the massaged kale.

Toss well until everything is evenly distributed and lightly coated in the vinaigrette.

Taste and serve: Taste the salad, then add more dressing as needed. I usually end up adding ALL OF IT, but you can stop when it tastes right to you. Give the salad one final toss, making sure there’s no dressing hiding at the bottom of the bowl, then serve!

Variations to Try

This easy kale salad is simple to customize. Swap out what you don’t like or adjust the flavors to suit your tastes. Here are a few of my favorite variations, along with some delicious ideas readers have shared:

  • Pears: Swap the Granny Smith apple for a ripe but firm pear for a softer texture and a little more sweetness.
  • Dried cranberries: Replace the raisins with dried cranberries for a slightly tarter flavor.
  • Different nuts: Use pecans, slivered almonds, or candied walnuts instead of plain walnuts. Pecans add a softer, buttery crunch, and almonds are a little firmer. Candied walnuts make the salad sweeter and I think they’d be especially good for fall or holiday meals!
  • Shredded carrots: Swap the raisins for shredded carrots if you hate raisins, but still want some added sweetness.
  • Cheese: Add shredded cheddar, crumbled feta, or shaved Parmesan for more richness and savory flavor.
  • Honey: Stir about 1 teaspoon of honey into the Dijon vinaigrette to soften the apple cider vinegar tang without making the dressing overly sweet.

Serving Suggestions

Once you’ve tossed everything together, you’re ready to dig into this easy kale salad! I’d happily eat it on its own for lunch, but it’s also really good with baked tofu cubes or sliced grilled chicken. In fact, grilled chicken is my top choice when I’m meal prepping this salad (see below!) Ooh, I also think our creamy pork chops would be so good here because apples and pork just belong together. That pairing would make an awesomely delicious dinner for a weeknight or even a special occasion. For another easy lunch option, pair it with an air fryer grilled cheese for a little crispy, melty goodness on the side.

Meal Prep it!

This fresh kale salad is one of my favorite salads to meal prep because kale holds up so well after it’s dressed. For a little extra insurance against browning, toss the chopped apples with a squeeze of lemon juice before adding them to the salad. Then divide the fully dressed salad into individual containers and refrigerate. It keeps well for up to 3-4 days! Add your favorite protein, like chicken, tofu, or drained and rinsed chickpeas, to make each portion a more filling grab-and-go lunch.

Storage Instructions

Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. There’s no need to keep the dressing separate, since the kale holds up well once dressed. Just note the leaves will continue to soften and the apples may lose a little crispness over time. The olive oil in the vinaigrette will also firm up in the fridge. I always let this salad sit at room temperature for a few minutes, then give it a good toss before serving again.

  • I’d make this Kale and Sweet Potato Salad for fall lunches because it keeps well in the fridge for about four days! 
  • This Crunchy Kale Chicken Salad is another way to turn sturdy kale into a filling meal-prep lunch with chicken, almonds, raisins, and creamy honey Dijon dressing.
  • Try my Kale Pasta Salad for a satisfying mix of tender kale, pasta, chickpeas, juicy tomatoes, Parmesan, and creamy balsamic dressing.

item.title: Bruschetta Chicken
item.dc:creator: Jennie Alley
item.description:
This easy Bruschetta Chicken recipe tops juicy pan-seared chicken with melty mozzarella, fresh tomatoes, basil, and balsamic glaze in just 25 minutes.

The post Bruschetta Chicken appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
This easy Bruschetta Chicken tops juicy, golden pan-seared chicken with melty mozzarella and a fresh, garlicky tomato-basil mixture, all in just 25 minutes. To help that pack of chicken go further, I slice two chicken breasts horizontally into four thinner portions. This also helps them cook super quickly in the skillet! The flavors in the bruschetta topping mingle while the chicken cooks, and there’s no chicken marinade to plan ahead for. At just $1.48 per serving, it’s a fresh, summery family dinner that delivers BIG flavor on a small budget. 😋

A Fast Skillet Dinner for Tomato Season

Bruschetta is one of my favorite appetizers, so piling all that fresh tomato goodness onto chicken just made sense! This recipe has some serious chicken Parmesan vibes, but instead of breading and marinara sauce, it gets a fresh topping made with tomatoes, basil, garlic, and balsamic vinegar. I also season the chicken with garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper, so there’s plenty of flavor underneath the melty mozzarella and juicy tomatoes.

I developed this as a stovetop skillet recipe, so it’s especially handy on hot days when the last thing I want to do is turn on the oven. The bruschetta mixture goes on after the chicken is cooked, which keeps the tomatoes fresh and juicy instead of letting them soften in the skillet. This method also works well for meal prep because I can store the chicken and topping separately and combine them when I’m ready to eat. Recipes like this make me thank my past self for buying chicken in bulk and freezing it!

Recipe Success Tips

  1. Chop the topping ingredients nice and small. Finely dice the red onion so its sharp flavor is spread throughout rather than overpowering one bite. I also like to cut the tomatoes into small, bite-sized pieces that are easy to scoop up with the chicken!
  2. Cut the chicken into even pieces. Chicken breasts are HUGE nowadays, so I slice each one in half horizontally to create four thinner portions. Try to make the pieces as even in thickness as possible. Evenly sized pieces will cook at roughly the same rate, giving you juicy chicken from edge to edge!
  3. Dry the chicken and heat the skillet properly. Pat each side of the chicken dry with paper towels before adding the seasonings. Then let the oil heat until it looks loose and glossy with a slight shimmer, but isn’t smoking. The chicken should give you an immediate, steady sizzle when it hits the pan. Wet chicken in a cool skillet will release moisture and steam instead of getting that delicious golden color. No one ordered boiled chicken here!
  4. Start checking the temperature early. Thin chicken cutlets cook fast, so I start checking my chicken after it’s cooked for about 3 minutes on the second side. Insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest part of each piece, coming in from the side if needed, and look for an internal temp of 165°F. Don’t rely on color alone because chicken can look done before the center is fully cooked.
  5. Turn the heat down when melting the cheese. Chicken breast can overcook quickly in a skillet. To avoid this, I finely shred the mozzarella so it melts faster and more predictably (compared to thick slices, pre-shredded, or fresh mozzarella!). I also turn the heat down to low before covering the skillet, then remove it from the heat as soon as the cheese has melted.

Bruschetta Chicken

This easy Bruschetta Chicken recipe tops juicy pan-seared chicken with melty mozzarella, fresh tomatoes, basil, and balsamic glaze in just 25 minutes.
Course Main Course
Cuisine American, Italian
Total Cost $5.93 serving / $1.48 recipe
Prep Time 10 minutes minutes
Cook Time 15 minutes minutes
Total Time 25 minutes minutes
Servings 4 servings
Calories 266kcal
Author Jennie Alley

Equipment

  • Medium Bowl
  • Large Skillet with Lid

Ingredients

  • 4 Roma tomatoes diced, (340g) $0.88
  • 3 garlic cloves minced, $0.27
  • 2 Tbsp red onion finely diced, (24g) $0.27
  • 2 Tbsp fresh basil thinly sliced, (julienned) (4g) $0.45
  • 2 Tbsp olive oil divided, (1 oz.) $0.35
  • 1 Tbsp balsamic vinegar see notes, $0.23
  • ½ tsp granulated sugar $0.01
  • 1¼ tsp salt divided, $0.10
  • ¾ tsp black pepper divided, (freshly cracked) $0.06
  • 1 lb. chicken breasts boneless & skinless, (2 breasts cut in half) $2.57*
  • 1 tsp garlic powder $0.03
  • ½ tsp Italian seasoning $0.02
  • ½ cup mozzarella cheese shredded, (60g) $0.47**
  • 1 Tbsp balsamic glaze for serving, (see notes) $0.22

Instructions

  • Gather and prep all ingredients.
  • In a medium bowl combine diced tomatoes, garlic, red onion and basil. Add 1 Tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar, sugar, ¼ tsp salt, and ¼ tsp black pepper. Mix well and set aside.***
  • Slice chicken breasts in half horizontally, pat dry and season with remaining 1 tsp of salt, ½ tsp of black pepper, garlic powder and italian seasoning.
  • Heat remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add chicken and cook for 3-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through with an internal temperature of 165°F.
  • Reduce heat to low and top each piece of chicken with about 2 Tbsp of shredded mozzarella. Cover with a lid (or foil) and cook for 2-4 minutes or until the cheese is melted.
  • Spoon the bruschetta mixture over the chicken and finish with a drizzle of balsamic glaze. Serve immediately and enjoy!

See how we calculate recipe costs here.

Notes

*Cutting the chicken breasts in half horizontally creates thinner pieces that cook quickly and evenly. I always buy value packs of chicken and freeze the breasts individually to make weeknight cooking easier and more budget-friendly. Cook the chicken to an internal temperature of 165°F (the center should look opaque and juicy with no pink meat).
**If you can, use freshly-shredded mozzarella for the smoothest melt! Pre-shredded cheese contains anti-caking agents that can affect the melt.
***Let the bruschetta mixture sit while the chicken cooks so the flavors develop and the tomatoes release their juices. Some of the juice will pool at the bottom of the bowl. You can spoon as much or as little of the liquid over each serving as you like. I’m team extra juice when there’s rice or pasta underneath to soak it up!
Use balsamic vinegar and balsamic glaze (they’re not the same thing!): Balsamic vinegar is a thin, dark vinegar made from grapes with a tangy slightly sweet flavor. Balsamic glaze is a thicker, sweeter reduction made with balsamic vinegar and sugar. They’re two different ingredients, and each serves a different purpose in this bruschetta chicken recipe. The vinegar flavors the tomato topping, and the glaze adds a sweet and tangy finishing drizzle. Use store-bought glaze or make our homemade balsamic glaze!

Nutrition

Serving: 1serving (1 piece of chicken) | Calories: 266kcal | Carbohydrates: 8g | Protein: 28g | Fat: 13g | Sodium: 951mg | Fiber: 1g

how to make Bruschetta Chicken Step-by-Step Photos

Gather all of your ingredients.

Mix the bruschetta topping: Add 4 diced Roma tomatoes, 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 Tbsp finely diced red onion, and 2 Tbsp thinly sliced fresh basil to a medium bowl. Pour in 1 Tbsp olive oil and 1 Tbsp balsamic vinegar, then add ½ tsp granulated sugar, ¼ tsp salt, and ¼ tsp freshly cracked black pepper. Gently stir until everything is well distributed. Set the mixture aside while you cook the chicken so the flavors have time to develop and the tomatoes can release some of their juices.

Slice and season the chicken: Place 1 lb. boneless, skinless chicken breasts (2 breasts) on a cutting board and slice each breast in half horizontally to create four thinner pieces. Try to keep them as even in thickness as possible so they cook at the same rate. Pat the chicken thoroughly dry with paper towels, then season with the remaining 1 tsp salt, remaining ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tsp garlic powder, and ½ tsp Italian seasoning.

Cook the chicken until golden: Add the remaining 1 Tbsp olive oil to a large skillet and heat it over medium-high. Now add the chicken pieces to the hot skillet in a single layer. You should hear a steady sizzle as soon as they touch the pan. Cook for 3-5 minutes without moving them, or until the bottoms develop golden-brown patches and release easily from the skillet.

Flip and cook for another 3-5 minutes. If the outside is browning too quickly, lower the heat slightly. Check the thickest part of each piece with an instant-read thermometer and cook until it reaches 165°F. The center should look opaque and juicy.

Add the cheese: Reduce the heat to low and divide ½ cup freshly shredded mozzarella over the four pieces of chicken, using about 2 Tbsp per piece.

Melt the cheese: Cover the skillet with a lid or foil and cook for 2-4 minutes, just until the cheese fully melts. Remove the skillet from the heat as soon as the mozzarella melts so the chicken doesn’t continue cooking and dry out.

Add the bruschetta topping: Give the tomato mixture another gentle stir, then spoon it over each piece of chicken. Add as much or as little of the flavorful juice from the bottom of the bowl as you like.

Finish with 1 Tbsp balsamic glaze drizzled over the top, then serve immediately while the chicken is hot, the cheese is melty, and the tomatoes are still fresh and juicy. Enjoy!

Serving Suggestions

This bruschetta chicken is basically begging for something to soak up all those garlicky tomato juices! It’s pictured above with our angel hair pasta pomodoro, and the delicate pasta and fresh tomato sauce keep the whole meal light and summery. For an even easier option, serve the chicken over cooked rice, quinoa, or plain pasta. A few slices of garlic bread are also never a bad idea for swiping the plate clean.

For a summery side, try my ditalini pasta salad. I load it with pesto, roasted summer vegetables, and feta, so it brings plenty of Italian-inspired flavor without piling on even more tomatoes. Our watermelon and feta salad is another fresh option with sweet watermelon, crisp cucumber, salty feta, fresh herbs, and balsamic glaze. For a lighter plate, serve the chicken over zucchini noodles, spaghetti squash, or cauliflower rice. However you build your plate, this chicken is a seriously delicious way to put summer produce to work!

Meal Prep it!

For meal prep, I like to store the chicken and bruschetta topping separately in airtight containers in the fridge so the tomatoes don’t make everything soggy. The topping will get juicier as it sits, which I personally don’t mind! But if you want to keep the liquid to a minimum, scoop out some of the tomato seeds before mixing the topping. Add the balsamic glaze just before serving so it stays glossy instead of disappearing into the container.

Storage & Reheating

Store leftover chicken and bruschetta topping separately in airtight containers in the fridge for 3-4 days. Keeping them apart prevents the juicy tomatoes from making the chicken soft and lets you reheat only what needs warming.

Reheating

Reheat the chicken gently in a skillet over low heat or in the microwave in short intervals until warmed through. Add the cold bruschetta topping and balsamic glaze just before serving to keep everything tasting fresh.

Freezing

You can freeze the seasoned, uncooked chicken in a freezer-safe container for up to 3 months, then thaw it overnight in the fridge before cooking. Cooked chicken can also be frozen, but leave off the bruschetta topping and make a fresh batch after thawing.

item.title: Baked Chicken Drumsticks
item.dc:creator: Beth Moncel
item.description:
These easy Baked Chicken Drumsticks need just 5 minutes of prep, pantry seasonings, and one sheet pan for juicy chicken with beautifully browned skin.

The post Baked Chicken Drumsticks appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
You guys know how I love easy dinner staples, right? These Baked Chicken Drumsticks are juicy and tender with deeply browned, crisp skin, and they only take about 5 minutes to prep! Just coat the chicken with seasoning, toss it in the oven, and focus on your side dishes or whatever else you have going on while they bake. I always check the thickest drumstick with a meat thermometer and cook it to 175°F for the juiciest dark meat. They’re easy, tasty, and the perfect “emergency” meal for when you don’t want to have to think about, “what’s for dinner?”

“Started making these several months ago. It’s now a regular go-to. So easy. So good. I’ve done a lot of cooking and usually enjoy it, but sometimes you just want something simple, uncomplicated, without a bunch of layers of “things”, Thanks for a great recipe and tips.”

Cindy

An Easy Dinner Win for Busy Nights

Bone-in chicken is almost always one of the most affordable cuts at the store, and drumsticks are especially great for tossing in the oven while you throw together some easy sides. I season mine with a simple mix of pantry spices (smoked paprika, garlic and onion powder, a little cayenne, oregano, salt, and pepper) plus oil, to help everything brown and crisp up in the oven. But if you want to switch up the seasonings or use a marinade, I’ve got more ideas below!

Drumsticks and thighs are both flavorful cuts of dark meat, but their shape affects how they cook. Drumsticks are smaller and more compact, while thighs are thicker and usually need a little more time in the oven. Bone-in, skin-on thighs are the best substitute for this recipe (if you don’t have drumsticks), but I still rely on the internal temperature rather than the clock to know when they’re done. For a quicker option, try our air fryer chicken drumsticks, which use similar seasonings but cook in almost half the time!

Recipe Success Tips

  1. Use a meat thermometer. I always use a meat thermometer to double-check my chicken is cooked through. Insert the thermometer into the thickest, meatiest part of the largest drumstick without touching the bone for the most accurate reading. Chicken is safe to eat once it reaches at least 165°F, but I cook drumsticks to about 175°F so the dark meat has time to become more tender.
  2. Start checking before the full cooking time is up. I usually begin checking the drumsticks at around 35 minutes, especially when they’re on the smaller side. Drumstick size, dark baking sheets, oven hot spots, and convection or countertop ovens can all affect how quickly the chicken cooks and browns.
  3. Flip them halfway through. To ensure even cooking and crispy skin, I always flip my drumsticks halfway through baking. It helps all sides to get golden brown and delicious!
  4. Don’t overcrowd the baking sheet. There should be enough space between each drumstick so hot air can circulate, and the skin can crisp up. I find the skin is more likely to stay soft when the pieces are packed too closely together. Use two baking sheets for a larger batch rather than squeezing everything onto one.
  5. Double the seasoning mix. If you use the spices in the recipe card, consider mixing a double batch before handling the raw chicken. Some of our readers have shared that this blend tastes amazing on roasted potatoes! I think it would be delicious on other roasted veggies, too. Keep the portion for your sides separate so it never comes into contact with raw chicken.
  6. Want to use chicken breasts? Dark meat chicken, like drumsticks and thighs, is extremely forgiving due to their higher fat content and the skin-on, bone-in combination that locks in moisture. Chicken breast needs a slightly different technique because it’s a leaner cut of meat. I only recommend swapping the drumsticks for bone-in, skin-on thighs when using the method in this recipe. For bone-in breasts, try my herb roasted chicken breast method instead, and for boneless skinless breasts, head to our baked chicken breasts recipe.
Print Add to Collection Go to Collections

Oven Baked Chicken Drumsticks

This oven-baked chicken drumstick recipe is the perfect dinner idea that can be flavored with any of your favorite seasonings.
Course Dinner, Main Course
Cuisine General
Total Cost $4.37 recipe / $0.73 serving
Prep Time 5 minutes minutes
Cook Time 40 minutes minutes
Total Time 45 minutes minutes
Servings 6 pieces
Calories 254kcal
Author Beth Moncel

Equipment

  • Enamelware Sheet Pan
  • Tongs
  • Meat Thermometer

Ingredients

  • 1 tsp smoked paprika $0.08
  • ½ tsp garlic powder $0.02
  • ¼ tsp onion powder $0.01
  • ⅛ tsp cayenne pepper $0.02
  • ¼ tsp dried oregano $0.02
  • ½ tsp salt $0.04
  • ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked, $0.04
  • 1.75 lbs. chicken drumsticks 6 pieces, $4.06*
  • 2 Tbsp cooking oil $0.08**

Instructions

  • Preheat the oven to 425ºF. Combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
  • Place the chicken drumsticks in a bowl and drizzle the cooking oil over top. Sprinkle the prepared seasoning over the drumsticks, then toss until they're evenly coated in oil and spices.
  • Place the seasoned drumsticks on a baking sheet with enough space around each so they're not touching. You can line the baking sheet with foil or parchment for easier cleanup, if desired.
  • Transfer the chicken to the oven and bake for 40 minutes, or until they reach an internal temperature of 175ºF, flipping the drumsticks once half-way through.*** Serve hot.

See how we calculate recipe costs here.

Video

Notes

*Use bone-in, skin-on chicken drumsticks for maximum flavor and juiciness. I used 6 drumsticks (about 1.75 lbs total). If you’re using more or less drumsticks, be sure to adjust the seasoning amounts accordingly. Smaller drumsticks may be ready before 40 minutes, so start checking them around 35 minutes. Extra-large pieces may need a few additional minutes. Use the internal temperature as your final guide. You can also swap in bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs using the same method as in this recipe.
**You can use any high-heat cooking oil, such as canola, vegetable, or avocado oil.
***Insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest part of the drumstick, making sure it doesn’t touch the bone. Chicken is safe to eat at 165°F, but I prefer cooking dark meat to about 175°F for a more tender result. If the drumsticks vary in size, check the temperature of more than one piece.
Air fryer method: To cook the drumsticks in an air fryer, preheat it to 400°F and arrange the chicken in a single layer without overlapping. Air fry for 12 minutes, flip, then cook for about 10 minutes more, or until the thickest piece reaches 175°F. Smaller drumsticks may cook faster, so begin checking them at around 18 minutes. See our air fryer chicken drumsticks for the full recipe. 
Seasoning notes: When substituting another seasoning blend, check whether it already contains salt and reduce or omit the added ½ teaspoon of salt as needed. Sugary sauces like barbecue or teriyaki can burn at high temperatures, so brush them over the drumsticks during the final 10-15 minutes of baking, if desired!

Nutrition

Serving: 1drumstick | Calories: 254kcal | Carbohydrates: 1g | Protein: 23g | Fat: 17g | Sodium: 332mg | Fiber: 0.2g

How to Make Chicken Drumsticks Step-by-Step Videos

Gather all of your ingredients and preheat the oven to 425ºF

Make the spice mix: Decide which herbs and spices you want to use to season the drumsticks. I used 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp garlic powder, ¼ tsp onion powder, ⅛ tsp cayenne pepper, ¼ tsp oregano, ¼ tsp freshly cracked black pepper, and ½ tsp salt.

Place about 1.75 lbs. chicken drumsticks in a large bowl and drizzle 2 Tbsp cooking oil over the top. Add the spice mixture, then toss until every drumstick has a thin, glossy coating and the spices are evenly distributed over the skin.

Bake the chicken: Arrange the drumsticks in a single layer on a baking sheet, leaving space between each piece so the hot air can circulate and the skin can crisp up and brown. Line the baking sheet with parchment paper for easier cleanup, if desired.

Bake for about 40 minutes. After about 20 minutes, the skin should be tightening and starting to brown. Flip each drumstick, then return the pan to the oven to finish cooking. The skin should look deeply browned and crisp around the edges once done. Insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest, meatiest part of the largest drumstick without touching the bone. Chicken is safe at 165°F, but I continue cooking drumsticks to about 175°F for more tender dark meat.

Serve hot and enjoy! (garnished with parsley for color, not needed for flavor)

Other Seasoning Ideas for Baked Chicken Drumsticks

I use a very classic mix of smoked paprika, garlic, onion, and oregano for this chicken drumsticks recipe, but you can literally use any seasoning blend you like for this. There’s so much flexibility! A dry seasoning blend is the quickest option because the chicken can go straight into the oven, but you can definitely marinate the chicken when there’s time to plan ahead. Here are some of my favorite options:

  • Ranch: Swap the spices for ranch seasoning when you want something herby, super savory, and very family-friendly. Ranch blends are often already salty, so I reduce or skip the added salt to keep the drumsticks from tasting over-seasoned.
  • Lemon pepper: I LOVE lemon pepper seasoning! It’s bright and peppery at the same time. Check the label before adding extra salt, though!
  • Garlic herb: My garlic herb seasoning keeps things simple with plenty of garlic and dried herbs, but without the smoky flavor from the paprika.
  • Taco: Taco seasoning gives the drumsticks a smoky, gently spicy flavor with warm cumin and chili powder.
  • Jerk: Jerk seasoning is the one to use when you want more heat, warm spices, and a bigger punch of flavor.
  • Teriyaki: Teriyaki sauce gives the drumsticks a sweet, salty, and savory glaze that’s totally different from the dry seasoning in the recipe card. I’d brush it on for 10-15 minutes toward the end of baking.
  • Greek yogurt marinade: The tangy yogurt, lemon, garlic, and herbs in my Greek chicken marinade adds flavor all the way around the chicken. That recipe is already written and tested for bone-in, skin-on drumsticks and thighs, so follow its marinade quantities and instructions instead of combining it with the dry spice blend here.

However, I promise a marinade isn’t required for juicy baked drumsticks! I always stick with the dry seasoning blend in this recipe when dinner needs to get into the oven quickly!

Serving Suggestions

This recipe makes about 6 oven roasted drumsticks, but you can easily scale that up depending on appetites! To keep dinner simple, I always serve them with budget-friendly favorites like creamy mashed potatoes, rice, or a side salad. I love our Instant Pot mashed potatoes because they take about the same amount of time as the chicken, but free up the stovetop so I can also make these quick lemon butter green beans. Both are pictured below with the plated chicken.

You can also add some oven roasted frozen broccoli to the baking sheet for the final 25-30 minutes, as long as there’s enough space around the chicken and broccoli for everything to roast. Stir the broccoli after about 20 minutes and check it a little early since the oven is set to 425°F. I think a dipping sauce would also be delicious! Some of my favorites are honey mustard, ranch dressing, or BBQ sauce (you can also brush the BBQ sauce over the chicken in the last 10-15 mins of baking!).

Storing and Reheating

Once cooled, store leftover cooked chicken drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

Reheating

I get the best results reheating these drumsticks in the oven or air fryer at 375°F until they’re heated through and the skin is crisp again. Check the thickest piece with a thermometer and make sure it reaches 165°F before serving. The microwave works in a pinch, but the skin will stay softer.

Freezing

Freeze the cooled drumsticks in a freezer-safe bag or container for up to 2-3 months. Thaw them overnight in the refrigerator, then reheat them in the oven or air fryer as above.

  • I always keep these Baked Chicken Breasts in my dinner rotation because they’re easy to prepare and go with almost any side.
  • Roasted Chicken and Vegetables combines juicy chicken thighs and caramelized vegetables in one cozy meal.

item.title: Cottage Cheese Eggs
item.dc:creator: Jess Rice
item.description:
These easy Cottage Cheese Eggs are soft, protein-packed, and made with just 4 ingredients. A quick 15-minute breakfast that’s perfect for busy mornings!

The post Cottage Cheese Eggs appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
These Cottage Cheese Eggs turn three everyday eggs into an extra-creamy breakfast using just four simple ingredients! A little cottage cheese works some serious breakfast magic here, giving every bite a soft texture and mild flavor I can’t get enough of. These cottage cheese eggs are ready in about 15 minutes, pack roughly 11 grams of protein per serving, and might just be the most delicious upgraded scrambled eggs you’ve ever had. 😉

Creamy Cottage Cheese Scrambled Eggs

I have chickens at home, so every time we crack an egg into a frying pan, I do a little happy dance. Raising chickens takes a lot of work, so it’s never lost on me what an incredible, nutrient-dense source of protein each little egg provides! Now, I know most of us don’t keep chickens at home (and I can tell you—it’s almost certainly more budget-friendly not to. Ha!). And I’m sure we all remember when egg prices skyrocketed and threw our grocery budgets into a total tailspin, but the great news is that egg prices have leveled out, making them once again a wonderfully affordable, high-quality protein staple. Pair that budget-friendly win with this recipe for cottage cheese eggs, and you truly can’t lose!

The addition of protein-packed cottage cheese is all it takes to make your classic scrambled eggs extra creamy and delicious. It’s protein added to protein! Which also means it’ll keep you FULL and doesn’t cost a ton, either! I add just a couple spoonfuls, which is enough to make the eggs soft and tender without adding too much moisture to the pan. I also like to gently mix in the cottage cheese so a few soft curds remain for a super creamy bite. Even if you’re not planning to hit the gym, this easy breakfast is going to make you very happy!

Recipe Success Tips

  1. Whisk the eggs really well! Beat the eggs and salt until the mixture is an even sunny yellow and looks slightly airy. This helps the eggs cook into softer, more uniform curds instead of leaving behind firm streaks of egg white.
  2. Adjust the heat to your stovetop. During testing, I found that my pan needed to be on the medium heat setting at our test kitchen, but medium-low was sufficient on my stovetop at home. If you feel like your cottage cheese scrambled eggs are taking too long to cook, and the texture is getting a little broken, kick the heat up a little and stop moving them around in the pan for a minute. Flip or stir once you see the eggs are cooking into more solid curds.
  3. Stir gently, then let the eggs cook. Use slow, sweeping motions to move the cooked egg aside and bring the liquid egg into contact with the pan. Try not to stir constantly, since the eggs need a few short pauses against the hot surface to form proper curds and allow excess moisture to cook away.
  4. Don’t mistake the cottage cheese for uncooked egg white! Because I add it after the eggs are fully whisked, a few small curds will be visible in the finished eggs. That texture is completely intentional and adds a creamy mouthfeel. If you prefer a totally smooth result, you can blend the egg mixture before cooking, but it’ll likely have a different texture than the version I’m sharing here.
Print Add to Collection Go to Collections

Cottage Cheese Eggs

These easy Cottage Cheese Eggs are soft, protein-packed, and made with just 4 ingredients. A quick 15-minute breakfast that’s perfect for busy mornings!
Course Breakfast
Cuisine American
Total Cost $0.58 recipe / $0.29 serving
Prep Time 5 minutes minutes
Cook Time 10 minutes minutes
Total Time 15 minutes minutes
Servings 2 servings
Calories 172kcal
Author Jess Rice

Equipment

  • Frying Pan

Ingredients

  • 3 large eggs $0.30
  • ⅛ tsp salt $0.01
  • 2 Tbsp cottage cheese $0.15*
  • 1 Tbsp butter $0.12

Instructions

  • Gather your ingredients.
  • Whisk the eggs well, and then whisk them some more! With a fork or a whisk, beat the eggs and salt together until the entire mixture is a consistent sunny yellow color, with no defined streaks of egg whites visible.
  • Add the cottage cheese.
  • Gently whisk the cottage cheese into the eggs, being careful to leave some of their natural texture intact. I think it adds to a pleasant mouthfeel to leave some of the curds!
  • Add butter to a skillet over medium-low heat. Once melted and a little foamy, add the cottage cheese egg mixture.
  • Be patient, let the eggs come up to temperature and begin to stir them in the pan once you see the color of your eggs turn from yellow to a more creamy bright yellow. Gently stir to move around the uncooked liquidy part of the egg to expose it to the pan. Don’t constantly stir, or you’ll end up with a sloppy mess. This doesn’t take long though, so don’t walk away!
  • Once the eggs are cooked, set but not tough or browning, remove them from the heat and enjoy!**

See how we calculate recipe costs here.

Notes

*You can use full-fat or low-fat cottage cheese, and either small or large curds will work. I always use 4% cottage cheese. If yours has a lot of liquid sitting on top, give it a quick stir or spoon off the excess before measuring.
**The eggs will continue cooking after you remove the pan from the heat. For softer, looser curds, take them off while they’re set but still slightly glossy.

Nutrition

Serving: 1serving | Calories: 172kcal | Carbohydrates: 1g | Protein: 11g | Fat: 13g | Sodium: 344mg

how to make Cottage Cheese Eggs Step-by-Step Photos

Gather all of your ingredients.

Whisk the eggs: Crack 3 large eggs into a medium bowl and add ⅛ tsp salt. Whisk thoroughly until the mixture is an even, sunny yellow with no visible streaks of egg white. Whisking well helps create softer, more evenly cooked eggs.

Add the cottage cheese: Add 2 Tbsp cottage cheese to the eggs (I use 4% cottage cheese).

Gently whisk just until it is distributed throughout the mixture. Leave some of the cottage cheese curds intact to give the finished eggs a soft and creamy texture.

Cook the eggs: Add 1 Tbsp butter to a nonstick skillet and place it over medium-low heat. Let the butter melt and become lightly foamy, but don’t let it brown. Pour the cottage cheese and egg mixture into the skillet. Let it sit undisturbed for several seconds, or until the eggs around the edges and across the bottom begin to turn from glossy yellow to a creamy, opaque yellow.

Gently scramble the eggs: Use a wooden spatula (or chopsticks!) to slowly push the cooked egg from the edges toward the center of the skillet. Tilt the pan slightly as needed so the uncooked egg can flow into the empty spaces and make contact with the hot surface. Stir only occasionally rather than continuously, which helps the eggs form soft, tender curds instead of becoming loose or mushy.

Continue gently folding and pushing the eggs around the skillet until they’re mostly set but still look slightly glossy and moist. This should only take a few minutes, so stay close to the stove!

Serve: Take the skillet off the heat before the eggs look completely dry, as they’ll continue cooking slightly from the residual heat. Serve your scrambled eggs with cottage cheese immediately, while they’re hot and delicious! Enjoy.

Serving Suggestions

I like to finish these cottage cheese scrambled eggs with a sprinkle of fresh chopped chives for a little extra flavor and color, but that’s totally optional. Sliced green onions, a crack of black pepper, or a few shakes of hot sauce are all great choices, too.

For a fuller breakfast, serve them with air fryer bacon, which cooks in about the same amount of time, along with fresh fruit or buttered toast (I love mine with tomato butter, personally!). A couple of reheated sheet pan pancakes are another fun option if you keep a batch tucked away in the freezer. Then add a glass of cold brew coffee, and breakfast is officially handled.

Storage & Reheating

These cottage cheese eggs are best when they’re freshly made. If you do have leftovers, let them cool, then transfer them to an airtight container and refrigerate for 3-4 days. I recommend making them fresh whenever possible, since scrambled eggs can become firmer once chilled and reheated.

Reheating

Reheat the eggs in the microwave in 20-30 second intervals, stirring between each one, until heated through. Keep a close eye on them, as reheating for too long can make the eggs overcooked and rubbery. Any leftover cottage cheese eggs would be delicious stirred into veggie fried rice for an easy dinner later in the day!

  • I’d fill these easy Cottage Cheese Wraps with hummus, roasted vegetables, and feta for an easy lunch!

item.title: 21 Tomato Recipes Worth Making While They’re in Season
item.dc:creator: Jess Rice
item.description:
These tomato recipes make the most of peak tomato season with easy salads, comforting soups, pasta dishes, and crowd-pleasing family meals.

The post 21 Tomato Recipes Worth Making While They’re in Season appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
I grow tomatoes at home every summer, but I’ll still happily grab a few extra at the farmers market or store when they look too good to leave behind. They’re sweeter, juicier, and usually much cheaper than they are the rest of the year, so now is the perfect time to make the most of them! Most of these dishes put fresh summer tomatoes front and center, but I’ve also included a few recipes that use canned tomatoes for good measure. You’ll find salads, hearty dinners, cozy soups, and easy dishes made for sharing, all proving tomatoes are good for far more than topping a salad!

Get More from Tomato Season!

  1. Shop with the season to save. Tomatoes are generally in season across the U.S. from June to September, when a larger local supply can mean lower prices at grocery stores and farmers’ markets. Exact timing will depend on the climate and variety. Early-season tomatoes (often smaller cherry varieties), mid-season tomatoes (including many Roma and slicer varieties), and late-season tomatoes (some heirloom tomatoes) can spread the harvest across summer and into early fall!
  2. Look for “seconds” and buy by the box. Farmers’ markets and farm stands often sell slightly bruised, cracked, or extra-ripe tomatoes for less because they’re not quite pretty enough for display. They may not be salad material, but they’re perfect for sauces, soups, salsa, and roasting!
  3. Store them the right way. Did you know you can buy (or pick!) tomatoes while they’re still a little green and let them ripen on the counter at room temperature? Just keep them away from direct sunlight! I like to store mine stem-side down because it helps protect the softer area around the stem and slows moisture loss. Avoid the refrigerator, since cold temperatures can dull their flavor and will change the texture. If this sounds familiar, you may have seen us share the same guidance over on our Instagram!

Hearty Dinners Featuring Tomatoes

Tomatoes deserve a whole lot more credit than just being a salad ingredient. They cook down into silky sauces, roast until they’re rich and jammy, and add brightness to everything from pasta to stuffed vegetables. These hearty dinner recipes all let tomatoes take center stage.

1. Creamy Tomato Spinach Pasta

Creamy Tomato and Spinach Pasta

Easier than a box meal, this creamy tomato and spinach pasta is also more flavorful and delicious. 100% real ingredients. Perfect for busy weeknights!
4.66 from 649 votes
$4.80 recipe / $1.20 serving Get the Recipe

Our quick-cooking creamy tomato spinach pasta is a great one to keep handy when summer dinner needs to stay simple. It comes together in about 30 minutes with pantry staples, and the tomatoes melt into a creamy sauce that coats the noodles. Toss in a few handfuls of spinach at the end, and you’ve got an easy weeknight dinner with barely any effort.

2. Angel Hair Pasta Pomodoro

Angel Hair Pasta Pomodoro

Angel Hair Pasta Pomodoro is an easy weeknight pasta recipe with tomatoes, olive oil, and herbs tossed with delicate noodles that cook in just 2 minutes!
4.80 from 10 votes
$5.21 recipe / $0.65 serving Get the Recipe

This angel hair pasta pomodoro is one of my favorite ways to let fresh tomatoes do what they do best. It has a short ingredient list, cooks quickly, and tastes wonderfully fresh thanks to ripe tomatoes, basil, garlic, and olive oil. I use angel hair because it cooks in just a few minutes, making this an easy way to turn in-season tomatoes into dinner.

3. Baked Feta Pasta

Baked Feta Pasta

This baked Feta Pasta recipe is made with budget-friendly roasted Roma tomatoes, onion, garlic, pasta, and a creamy block of feta! Easy and SO delicious!
4.86 from 7 votes
$11.05 recipe / $2.76 serving Get the Recipe

My version of feta pasta keeps the viral favorite budget-friendly by using Roma tomatoes, but you can definitely use cherry or plum tomatoes if you’ve got them growing at home! The tomatoes roast until sweet and juicy, creating a creamy sauce with almost no extra work. Once everything is soft and bubbling, just stir it together and toss it with the pasta.

4. Tuscan White Bean Stuffed Tomatoes

Tuscan White Bean Stuffed Tomatoes

This Tuscan White Bean Stuffed Tomatoes recipe is hearty, warming, and deeply satisfying. It's also budget-friendly and easy to make!
4.41 from 10 votes
$9.42 recipe / $2.35 serving Get the Recipe

If you’ve never tried my Tuscan white bean stuffed tomatoes, prepare to be surprised by how filling they are. I packed the stuffing with white beans, four types of veggies, herbs, and Parmesan, so every tomato becomes a complete meal. They’re certainly hearty enough for dinner but still feel fresh and summery!

5. Tomato Pie

Tomato Pie

This homemade tomato pie recipe is the perfect way to use up fresh summer tomatoes. It's creamy and tangy, and the leftovers are fantastic!
4.46 from 22 votes
$14.14 recipe / $1.76 serving Get the Recipe

When tomato season is in full swing, I always make at least one tomato pie. Juicy summer tomatoes, fresh basil, a tangy cheese and mayonnaise filling, and a flaky puff pastry crust come together to make one seriously delicious slice. It’s perfect for brunch, lunch, or an easy summer dinner, and I think the leftovers are even better the next day.

Tomato Soup Recipes

Soup might not be the first thing that comes to mind during tomato season, but it’s one of the best ways to use a generous haul! These recipes range from quick and comforting to chilled and refreshing, with several that can be frozen for another day.

6. Roasted Tomato Soup

Roasted Tomato Soup

Roasted tomato soup is made with fresh tomatoes, onions, and garlic that are slowly roasted until the flavors are deep, sweet, and cozy!
4.43 from 14 votes
$8.62 recipe / $2.16 serving Get the Recipe

Roasting makes all the difference in this roasted tomato soup. The tomatoes caramelize in the oven, which concentrates their sweetness and gives the soup a deep, rich flavor that fresh tomatoes alone can’t match. If you prefer a creamy bowl, I’d stir in a splash of heavy cream, half-and-half, or coconut milk before serving.

7. Tomato Lentil Soup

Tomato Lentil Soup

This tomato lentil soup is full of vegetables and herbs for a simple, flavorful, and warming winter soup. Makes great leftovers!
4.92 from 49 votes
$4.74 recipe / $0.79 serving Get the Recipe

Tomato lentil soup is one of those recipes I come back to because it’s comforting without taking all afternoon to make. Red lentils cook quickly, naturally thicken the soup, and add plenty of plant-based protein to make it satisfying enough for lunch or dinner!

8. Salmorejo

Salmorejo

Salmorejo is a cold Spanish soup that's delicious, creamy, easy to make, and a great way to use up summer tomatoes and day-old bread! On a hot summer day, it's pure tangy, velvety, perfection.
3.75 from 4 votes
$9.78 recipe / $1.22 serving Get the Recipe

Cold soup might sound unusual at first, but salmorejo makes total sense once summer is in full swing. Tomatoes, crusty bread, garlic, olive oil, and vinegar blend into a velvety soup that feels surprisingly substantial for such a short ingredient list. I’d definitely serve it well chilled on the hottest days.

9. Swamp Soup

Swamp Soup Recipe

A thick, tomatoey vegetable soup with "swampy" bits of spinach and gooey swiss cheese make this unconventional Swamp Soup unforgettable!
4.65 from 53 votes
$11.44 recipe / $1.43 serving Get the Recipe

Our swamp soup is basically tomato soup with the volume turned all the way up. Tomato sauce and diced tomatoes make the broth thick and hearty, frozen spinach adds plenty of vegetables with no chopping, and those gooey cubes of Swiss cheese are hands down the best part. It’s ready in about 30 minutes and makes eight servings, so it’s a great one for feeding a family or stocking the freezer.

10. Sopa de Letras

Sopa De Letras

Sopa De Letras, or alphabet soup, is a delicious and hearty tomato-based Mexican soup that's packed with flavor and ready in twenty!
4.59 from 12 votes
$6.70 recipe / $0.84 serving Get the Recipe

My daughter would be all over the alphabet pasta in sopa de letras, but I’m here for how quick and affordable it is. Roma tomatoes, onion, garlic, and vegetable broth are blended into the base, then the pasta is toasted before simmering, so it gets a little extra flavor. The whole pot is ready in just 20 minutes!

Fresh & Easy Summer Favorites

Tomatoes are one of my favorite budget ingredients when they’re in season because they can go in just about anything. These recipes stretch a few ripe ones into salads, sandwiches, salsa, and dressing with very little fuss.

11. Cucumber Tomato Salad

Cucumber Tomato Salad

This Cucumber Tomato Salad is a cold, crunchy, juicy mix of cucumbers, tomatoes, bell pepper, red onion, parsley, and feta tossed in a simple red wine oregano vinaigrette.
4.17 from 95 votes
$6.62 recipe / $1.10 serving Get the Recipe

Fresh tomatoes and crisp cucumbers were made for each other, and our cucumber tomato salad proves it. The simple vinaigrette lets the vegetables do the talking, and it pairs with just about anything coming off the grill!

12. Tomato Sandwiches

Tomato Sandwiches

Tomato sandwiches are a summertime staple. With juicy ripe tomatoes, creamy mayonnaise, and soft bread, they're a simple summer delight!
4.89 from 17 votes
$1.32 each Get the Recipe

I made these classic tomato sandwiches for lunch the other day, and they reminded me how good simple food can be. A perfectly ripe tomato, soft bread, mayonnaise, and plenty of black pepper really don’t need much else. 😋

13. Pico de Gallo

Pico de Gallo

This fresh and easy pico de gallo only takes a few minutes to make and adds vibrant flavor to your tacos, enchiladas, nachos, and more.
5 from 4 votes
$4.18 recipe / $0.35 serving Get the Recipe

There is almost always a bowl of pico de gallo in my fridge whenever we’re making tacos, burritos, or nachos. It’s fresh, easy to throw together, and tastes even better after the flavors mingle for a little while. Any leftovers disappear quickly around my house.

14. Caprese Salad

Caprese Salad

Nothing screams summer more than Caprese salad made with juicy, ripe tomatoes, creamy mozzarella cheese, and sweet and spicy basil!
5 from 1 vote
$13.93 recipe / $2.32 serving Get the Recipe

For me, a caprese salad tastes like summer in a bowl. Sweet tomatoes, creamy fresh mozzarella, fragrant basil, and a drizzle of balsamic create the perfect balance of juicy, creamy, fresh, and tangy in every forkful. I think it’s one of those recipes that proves great ingredients don’t need much help!

15. Avocado and Tomato Salad

Avocado and Tomato Salad

This simple avocado and tomato salad is a chunky mix of all of summer's fresh flavors, like tomato, avocado, lime, and cilantro.
4.17 from 6 votes
$6.13 recipe / $1.02 serving Get the Recipe

Think of our avocado and tomato salad as an extra chunky guacamole packed with fresh vegetables. The avocado makes it creamy, and the tomatoes, cucumber, and onion keep everything crisp and refreshing. It tastes best the day it’s made, but if you press plastic wrap directly onto the surface before refrigerating, the avocado stays greener for longer!

16. Tomato Basil Vinaigrette

Tomato Basil Vinaigrette

This tangy and slightly sweet tomato basil vinaigrette only requires a few simple ingredients and tastes great over salad and pasta alike.
5 from 7 votes
$1.34 recipe / $0.34 serving Get the Recipe

item.title: Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers
item.dc:creator: Melissa Nolan
item.description:
This Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers recipe is loaded with tender chicken, spicy buffalo sauce, cheddar, and blue cheese. An easy AND delicious dinner!

The post Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers appeared first on Budget Bytes.
item.content:encoded:
These Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers are my favorite workaround for turning creamy buffalo chicken dip into a totally acceptable weeknight dinner. This recipe starts with fresh diced chicken breast that I pan-sear, then fold into a buttery hot sauce mixture with cream cheese, cheddar, and a sprinkle of blue cheese for a classic buffalo flavor. The creamy, spicy filling gets piled into budget-friendly green bell pepper halves, baked until bubbly, and finished with green onions for a fresh bite. They’re ooey, gooey, salty, spicy, knock-your-socks-off delicious, and totally satisfying as a full meal!

Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Bell Peppers

Something you should know about me: I LOVE a good dip. I know it’s slightly frowned upon to make a dip your entire dinner, so I creatively came up with this buffalo chicken stuffed peppers recipe. Boom, problem solved. It takes everything I adore about buffalo chicken dip and makes it more ‘socially acceptable’ to eat as a full meal. I make everything from scratch in this recipe, starting with searing the chicken, so you don’t need to rely on leftovers or rotisserie chicken if you don’t already have it.

Once the chicken is seared, I turn it into a creamy buffalo filling with hot sauce, butter, cream cheese, garlic powder, onion powder, and plenty of cheddar. I follow our classic stuffed peppers recipe here and use halved bell peppers because it’s such a budget-friendly way to make whole peppers go further. Finish the peppers with blue cheese crumbles and fresh green onions, and if you’re a buffalo chicken fan like me, you won’t hesitate for a second to call this dinner.

Recipe Success Tips

  1. Stretch your peppers into multiple servings. I use 3 large green bell peppers and slice them in half lengthwise to make 6 servings, which keeps the cost down without making the portions feel skimpy. The halves also lay flat in the baking dish, which makes them SO much easier to fill!!
  2. Pat and drain the chicken. I pat the chicken dry before searing so it browns instead of steams, then drain it on paper towels after cooking to keep the filling from turning watery.
  3. Dice the chicken small and evenly. I keep the chicken pieces small, so they cook through quickly in the skillet. Even pieces also mix into the sauce better, so the filling tastes like creamy buffalo chicken all the way through. The internal temperature of the chicken should reach 165°F before serving.
  4. Lower the heat before making the sauce. Medium-high heat is great for searing the chicken, but I turn it down to medium before adding the butter, hot sauce, and cream cheese so the sauce melts together smoothly.
  5. Add extra veggies if you want to bulk them up. Sauté mushrooms or onions after the chicken comes out of the skillet, or stir in peas or corn with the cooked chicken before stuffing the peppers.

Time-Saving Tip

Cooking the chicken yourself is usually the cheapest option, and that’s why I wrote the recipe this way. But listen, time is valuable too! If it’s one of those nights, grab a rotisserie chicken and keep moving. Cold rotisserie chickens are often cheaper than hot ones, so check that section first if your store has both.

This recipe uses 1½ lbs. of raw chicken breast, which equals about 3 cups of cooked diced or shredded chicken. Just skip the searing step, stir the cooked chicken into the buffalo sauce until it’s warmed through, then stuff the peppers and bake as written.

Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers

This Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers recipe is loaded with tender chicken, spicy buffalo sauce, cheddar, and blue cheese. An easy AND delicious dinner!
Course Main Course
Cuisine American
Total Cost $11.45 recipe / $1.91 serving
Prep Time 15 minutes minutes
Cook Time 45 minutes minutes
Total Time 1 hour hour
Servings 6 servings
Calories 389kcal
Author Melissa Nolan

Equipment

  • 8×10 Casserole Dish
  • Large 12" skillet

Ingredients

  • nonstick cooking spray $0.01
  • 1½ lb. chicken breasts small dice, (2 breasts, 680g) $4.00*
  • ¼ tsp salt $0.01
  • ½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked, $0.08
  • 1 Tbsp vegetable oil $0.04
  • 3 large green bell peppers cut lengthwise & seeds removed, $2.46**
  • 1 Tbsp butter $0.11
  • ½ cup hot sauce 4oz., $1.29***
  • ½ tsp garlic powder $0.02
  • ½ tsp onion powder $0.02
  • 4 oz. cream cheese cubed, $0.91
  • 1½ cups cheddar cheese grated & divided, (150g) $1.18****
  • ¼ cup blue cheese 45g, $1.20*****
  • 2 green onions sliced, $0.12

Instructions

  • Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8×10-inch casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray and set it aside.
  • Dice the chicken into small pieces and pat dry with paper towels. Season the chicken evenly with salt and pepper.
  • Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the cubed chicken in an even layer. Sear in batches if needed. Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Remove the chicken from the skillet and place it on paper towels to drain. Set aside.
  • Turn the heat to medium and add the butter, hot sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, and cream cheese. Stir until the cream cheese has melted, about 2 minutes.
  • Add 1 cup of cheddar cheese and the diced chicken back into the pan. Fold until it melts and combine for about 1 minute. Then turn off the heat.
  • Place the bell peppers in the casserole dish, cut side up. Fill each pepper with the buffalo chicken filling.
  • Bake the peppers, uncovered, in the oven for 20 minutes. Remove them from the oven, then evenly top with the remaining cheddar cheese and blue cheese.
  • Place them back in the oven and continue cooking for an additional 15 minutes. Top with green onions, then enjoy!

See how we calculate recipe costs here.

Notes

*Boneless, skinless chicken thighs also work well in this recipe and will add a slightly richer flavor since they’re fattier than chicken breasts. They may need an extra minute or two in the skillet, and I’d still drain them on paper towels before adding them to the sauce. You can also use about 3 cups leftover cooked diced, or shredded chicken. Skip the searing step and stir the cooked chicken into the buffalo sauce until warmed through.
**I use green bell peppers because I love the taste and price! Feel free to use any color, or even try poblano peppers if you want to. Red, yellow, and orange peppers are all sweeter than green peppers, but will still be delicious here.
***I love and use Frank’s Red Hot Original hot sauce, and it’s got a kick! It has about a medium heat level. Feel free to use a less (or more) spicy hot sauce, or your favorite!
****Cheddar cheese is great here because it melts easily, and adds a sharp flavor. Mozzarella, provolone, Mexican cheese blend, or a mix of cheeses will also work if that’s what you have on hand.
*****I really love blue cheese, and it’s pretty traditional for buffalo chicken recipes. I know many people don’t love blue cheese, so feel free to omit it or use feta, goat cheese, or another cheese of your choice as an alternative. You can also serve these buffalo chicken stuffed peppers with a bottle of blue cheese dressing, and let everyone add their own.

how to make Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Peppers Step-by-Step Photos

Gather all of your ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease an 8×10-inch casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray and set it aside.

Prep the chicken: Start by dicing 1½ lbs. chicken breasts into small, even pieces. Try to keep the pieces a similar size so they cook at the same rate.

Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then season evenly with ¼ tsp salt and ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper. Patting the chicken dry helps it get a nice sear in the skillet.

Brown the chicken: Heat 1 Tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot and shimmering, add the diced chicken in an even layer. Sear in batches if needed so the chicken browns evenly. Cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then flip and cook for another 3 minutes, or until the chicken is lightly browned. Transfer the chicken to a paper towel-lined plate to drain and set aside.

Make the buffalo sauce: Turn the heat down to medium. Add 1 Tbsp butter, ½ cup hot sauce, ½ tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp onion powder, and 4 oz. cubed cream cheese to the skillet. Stir constantly until the butter and cream cheese melt into a smooth, creamy buffalo sauce, about 2 minutes.

Finish the filling: Add 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese and the cooked chicken back to the skillet. Fold everything together until the cheese is melted and the chicken is coated in the creamy buffalo sauce, about 1 minute. Turn off the heat.

Stuff the peppers: Place 3 large green bell peppers (cut in half lengthwise with the seeds removed), cut-side up in the prepared casserole dish. Nestle them close together so they stay steady while baking. Divide the buffalo chicken filling evenly between the 6 pepper halves, gently mounding the filling as needed.

Bake: Place the baking dish in the oven and bake the buffalo chicken stuffed peppers uncovered for 20 minutes, or until the filling is hot and the peppers are beginning to soften but still hold their shape.

Add more cheese: Remove the dish from the oven. Sprinkle the peppers evenly with the remaining ½ cup shredded cheddar cheese and ¼ cup blue cheese crumbles.

Return the dish to the oven and bake for another 15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the peppers are tender.

Finish: Now top your peppers with 2 sliced green onions, then serve. Enjoy!

Serving Suggestions

Each serving is one pepper half, so I like to add a simple side to round these buffalo chicken stuffed peppers out for dinner. Rice is my favorite budget-friendly pick because it stretches the meal and catches any extra creamy buffalo filling that sneaks out of the peppers. For something heartier, roasted potatoes, potato wedges, or sweet potato fries all give you a cozy plate without much extra work. For something fresh, go with a salad that can stand up to the spicy, cheesy filling. My easy green bean salad adds crunch and a bright, tangy bite. I also love our strawberry spinach salad here as it brings a natural sweetness that plays so well with buffalo sauce. A few celery and carrot sticks also keep things cool and crunchy!

Prep Them Ahead!

You can prep these buffalo chicken stuffed peppers ahead of time! I like to make the buffalo chicken filling first, let it cool, then store it in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. You can also slice and clean the bell peppers ahead of time and store them in the fridge.

For the best texture, I’ll assemble the peppers right before baking. If you want to fully assemble them ahead, let the filling cool, then stuff the peppers, and cover the baking dish and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Bake as directed, adding a few extra minutes as they’re going into the oven cold.

Storage & Reheating

Store any cooled leftover peppers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3-4 days.

Reheating

Reheat the buffalo chicken stuffed peppers in the microwave until warmed through, or place them in a 350°F oven until hot.

Freezing

You can freeze these buffalo peppers, but they’ll soften more after thawing and reheating. Freeze them in an airtight freezer-safe container for up to 2-3 months, then thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

  • I’ll serve these classic Stuffed Bell Peppers when I want something comforting that already has the meat, vegetables, and rice in one dish!
